title: M5-C transfer, callback and settlement implementation is absent
behavior: Current code is byte-identical to recorded M5-B. begin_native_preflight consumes consent and writes PreflightPending, but returns without any token/storage promise. No native dispatch, private callbacks, promise-result handling or reserved-to-spent completion exists. Enum variants alone do not implement transitions.
reproduction: Compare current source hashes to m5b-implementation-results.json: all native implementation/test files match.
Inspect src/native.rs:368-416 and search executable source for Promise construction, ft_transfer call, private callbacks and promise-result inspection. None exists.
Build candidate and inspect generated ABI and actual WASM exports: 14 native foundation methods; no transfer/callback/success method.
Run native::tests::independent_approval_preflight_consumption_and_no_accounting_or_promises: it passes by asserting zero receipts and spent0.
impact: Native payouts cannot execute or settle. The M5-C security conclusion cannot be established; advancing as though C were complete would rely on nonexistent controls.
remediation: In a separately authorized local implementation stage, implement the approved storage-preflight→fixed ft_transfer→private callback graph, atomic locks, outcome handling and exactly-once settlement; then repeat adversarial review. Do not add a public manual-success override.

title: Public preflight consumes approval into a lock with no continuation
behavior: An authorized B preflight writes Consumed/PreflightPending with no promise and no public continuation, failure, release or retry path. This is intentional B staging, not a hidden token-transfer bug.
reproduction: Observe Consumed auth, native PreflightPending, legacy Reserved and reserved100000/spent0.

Try repeated preflight, new authorization and revocation: all reject; no receipt exists to finish execution. Existing test native::tests::duplicate_pending_attempts_unknown_payout_and_cross_payout_auth_reject covers these rejections.
impact: If this foundation were deployed/used as an executor, the reservation would remain locked without delivery. This demonstrates missing liveness, not duplicate transfer or accounting corruption.
remediation: M5-C must join state consumption with storage-promise scheduling atomically. Keep uncertain attempts locked; do not solve liveness by enabling arbitrary reset/release or fake success.

title: No asynchronous receipt, callback-failure or gas validation exists
behavior: 126 passing tests are direct Rust/SDK environment tests. There are no native callbacks, promise-result injection tests, sandbox harness, transfer receipts, callback OOG measurements or gas constants/guards. Future terminal phases are inserted directly into test storage, not reached via token execution.
reproduction: Inspect the tests and Cargo manifest; search for near-workspaces/sandbox/promise_result/PromiseResult/private callbacks/static gas.
Inspect native::tests::pending_manual_review_and_terminal_states_cannot_approve_revoke_or_restart: private test code seeds future states.
Inspect test-framework.json: no near-sandbox executable on PATH, no repository sandbox harness. No dependencies were installed or mocks substituted.
impact: No evidence supports exactly-once delivery, callback authentication, failure atomicity, receipt interleaving, or sufficient nested gas budgets.
remediation: After implementing C, add real local receipt execution with a conforming mock token and controlled failures, measure each receipt, and test successful transfer with callback panic/OOG and blocked resend. Distinguish mock-result unit tests from sandbox receipts.

title: Historical mock-state compatibility does not prove full WASM upgrade safety
behavior: Authentic fixture has zero payouts and is loaded into SDK mock storage. Nonempty settlement/failure/index state is locally generated with current legacy functions. No old-WASM→candidate-WASM sandbox upgrade, token custody migration or live migration was executed.
reproduction: Run authentic_deployed_bytes_deserialize_and_bootstrap_preserves_every_legacy_entry and inspect its explicit pause before byte-comparison baseline.
Inspect nonempty_legacy_payout_indexes_failure_settlement_and_resolution_survive_bootstrap: synthetic fixture strips new native namespaces, then bootstraps in Rust.
Verify no sandbox harness or live upgrade evidence exists in the current candidate.
impact: Byte compatibility is supported, but protocol-level upgrade/receipt behavior and token preservation remain unproven. No demonstrated serialization corruption was found.
remediation: Keep M5-E as a mandatory deployment blocker: old/final candidate WASM, fresh authentic raw snapshot plus representative nonempty states, interrupted/unauthorized/repeated bootstrap, token custody and callback compatibility. Never assume older-WASM rollback is safe.

title: Recipient approval is a governance attestation and token/root trust is unresolved
behavior: Recipient enrollment checks a 64-character digest and exclusions, not NEP413 control, account existence, token storage or balance. Token ID is fixed but its transfer implementation is not exercised. Role separation does not eliminate root/governance control.
reproduction: Read approve_native_recipient and its tests: local evidence hash is synthetic, no token call.
Inspect fixed token/domain and role setters: on-chain address separation exists, human independence is operational.
impact: No actual controlled recipient or trustworthy live-delivery route is established. A future successful promise from a malicious/no-op token would not by itself prove economic delivery.
remediation: Before live gates, independently verify recipient control/key membership, storage and initial balance; review token code/governance/restrictions and root-key safeguards. Keep receipt/balance attribution independent. No changes authorized by this review.
